conflict_topics: Who will complete Agent D's unfinished section for the Thursday pitch
Whether Agent D should work during bereavement (attend family events vs complete work)
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants speak in natural, role-consistent ways; expressions of condolences are concise and appropriate (Turn 1, 4).
Several turns repeat the same refusal ('I can't' / 'I have no time. Zero.' Turns 8, 17, 19, 21, 23), producing some repetition.
Positions are grounded with reasons: B cites covering another colleague; C cites unfamiliarity and being behind; A cites client expectations and team responsibility.
No factual or role confusion; the timeline and constraints (wake/funeral, Thursday deadline) remain consistent throughout.
evaluation.final_reason: No mutual agreement was reached. Agent B and Agent C repeatedly refused to take on additional work ('I can't... I'm already covering...' Turn 8; 'I can't... I'm already behind' Turn 23; 'I have no time. Zero.' Turn 21). Agent D offered to work after the wake ('I can work on it tonight,' Turn 11; Turn 24), but Agent A explicitly forbade that and insisted the team cover the work ('no. You need to be with your family. Don't even think about work tonight.' Turn 12; 'This is not an option. We are not letting Agent D work.' Turn 25). No concrete, mutually accepted allocation was agreed upon, so the substantive disagreement remains.
position_change_notes: Agent D: Initially stated they 'need to be there with my family' (Turn 2) but later offered to work after the wake ('I can work on it tonight,' Turn 11; Turn 24). This is a substantive position change toward taking on the task.
Agent A: Consistently pushed for team coverage and strongly opposed Agent D working late into bereavement (Turn 12; Turn 25). A offers solutions (division of labor) but has not secured acceptance.

Agent B: Consistently refused to take on more work, citing lack of capacity and prior coverage responsibilities ('I can't... I'm already covering...' Turn 8; 'I have no time. Zero.' Turn 21). No softening observed.
Agent C: Consistently refused as well, citing unfamiliarity with analysis and being behind on their own section (Turn 10; Turn 23). No change toward accepting extra work.

round_scores.evidence: Agent D announces a death and need to be with family; others offer condolences (Turn 1-2). No incompatible demands expressed.
Agent A says 'Don't worry about the pitch, we'll figure it out' (Turn 3). Still cooperative; no one objects.
Agent A signals the need to figure out coverage for Agent D's section (Turn 7). Planning begins but no disagreement expressed yet.

Agent B states they can't take on anything more because they're already covering another colleague (Turn 8). This introduces a clear disagreement between the expectation that teammates will cover the work and B's inability to do so.

Agent C also refuses ('I can't... I've never done that kind of analysis' Turn 10) while Agent D offers to work tonight after the wake (Turn 11). Multiple incompatible positions now exist (team cover vs B/C refusal vs D offering to work).

Agent A insists D must not work and be with family ('no. You need to be with your family. Don't even think about work tonight.' Turn 12) while Agent D replies that it has to be done and asks who will do it (Turn 13). Direct opposition intensifies.
Agent A says the three of them will figure it out (Turn 14) but Agent B repeats they can't (Turn 15). Positions persist: A expects team coverage; B refuses; D previously offered to work.
Agent A proposes a three-way split of the remaining work (Turn 16); Agent B reiterates inability to take on more ('I can't do it.' Turn 17). The disagreement over who will do the work continues.
Agent A presses that 'can't' won't get the pitch done and demands a plan (Turn 18); Agent B continues to state they can't (Turn 19). No resolution or compromise achieved.

Agent A offers a concrete split (A will take analysis; B and C split data/sources) (Turn 20), and Agent B forcefully repeats they have 'no time. Zero.' (Turn 21). Disagreement over capacity remains firm.

Agent C says they still can't because they're behind on their own part (Turn 23). At this point both B and C refuse additional work; A remains willing to absorb analysis but no mutual agreement; D earlier offered to do it himself.

Agent D reiterates they'll work tonight (Turn 24). Agent A responds with a firm prohibition ('no. Absolutely not... This is not an option. We are not letting Agent D work.' Turn 25) and demands a plan from the three. The incompatible demands (A: team covers and forbids D working; B/C: won't take extra work; D: will do the work) remain unresolved and more sharply expressed.

substantive_insights: Tension is between compassionate leave expectations and the practical need to meet a near-term deadline.

Capacity is constrained: two teammates explicitly cannot take on more, so the feasible options are (a) A takes extra work alone, (b) D works during bereavement, or (c) external help—only (a) or (b) possible but neither has mutual acceptance.
Agent D's position shifts from prioritizing family (initially) to volunteering to work, reflecting pressure from the looming deadline.
Agent A emphasizes collective responsibility and protects D from working, but lacks the agreement of B and C to implement that protection.
